sections.h2: Where is Tooele County and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Tooele County sits in northwestern Utah, west of Salt Lake County, and covers 7,286 square miles, of which 6,941 are land. That makes it the second largest county in the state, and one of the driest.

Most of the people live in a strip along the east edge. The Oquirrh Mountains separate Tooele Valley from the Salt Lake Valley, the Stansbury Mountains run parallel to them, and Rush Valley lies to the south behind a low rise called the Stockton Bar. The western half belongs to the Great Salt Lake Desert, with the Bonneville Salt Flats crossed by Interstate 80. Skull Valley, between the Cedar and Stansbury ranges, holds the Skull Valley Indian Reservation and Dugway Proving Ground.

The county borders Box Elder, Davis, Salt Lake, Utah and Juab counties in Utah, plus Elko and White Pine counties in Nevada. For a seller, the practical point is that two houses with the same Tooele County mailing address can sit in very different settings, from a town lot in Tooele to acreage on the edge of the desert, and the assessor values them separately.

sections.h2: Which towns and areas make up the county?
sections.html:
Tooele is the county seat and the largest city, followed by Grantsville, with smaller communities such as Erda, Lake Point, Stockton, Rush Valley, Wendover and Ibapah scattered across the county.

  • Tooele: 35,742 residents in 2020, on the western slope of the Oquirrhs at about 4,915 feet. It was incorporated on June 19, 1853, and sits roughly 40 minutes from Salt Lake City.
  • Grantsville: 12,617 residents in 2020 at about 4,265 feet, incorporated January 12, 1867. State Route 138 runs through town toward Interstate 80 and east to Stansbury Park.
  • Stansbury Park: 9,851 residents in 2020, up from 5,145 in 2010. It is unincorporated, so the county provides most services, and it is about six miles north of Tooele on State Route 36.
  • Wendover: 1,115 residents in 2020, directly across the line from West Wendover, Nevada.

Stansbury Park deserves a note for sellers. It began in 1970 as a planned community with a golf course and a man-made lake, water and sewer come from the Stansbury Park Improvement District, and the Stansbury Park Community Association gives preliminary approval to housing and remodeling plans. If you own there, a buyer will ask about association rules early.

sections.h2: What drives the Tooele County economy?
sections.html:
Mining, defense and industrial work have shaped Tooele County since the 1860s, and a growing share of residents now commute to the Salt Lake Valley.

The employers named in the Tooele city entry include Kennecott Utah Copper, which runs the Bingham Canyon Mine on the far side of the Oquirrhs, US Magnesium, EnergySolutions at Clive, a Cabela's distribution center, and government at the federal, state and county level. The former Tooele Army Depot land now hosts the Tooele Industrial Depot, a group of manufacturers, warehouses and offices. Grantsville points to a new Walmart distribution center and the Utah Motorsports Campus as nearby draws.

sections.h2: What does the weather mean for a Tooele County house?
sections.html:
Tooele sees hot dry summers and cold winters with real snow, so roofs, heating systems and exterior paint take steady wear.

The Tooele climate summary lists normal highs of 38.7 degrees in January and 91.4 degrees in July, about 18.44 inches of precipitation a year and 75.3 inches of snowfall. The record high is 106 degrees and the record low is minus 16. Grantsville gets lake-effect snow from the Great Salt Lake only occasionally, and Wendover averages about 4.58 inches of precipitation, which makes it the driest spot in the Great Basin.

A buyer's inspector in this county will look first at the roof, the furnace and the water heater, then at settling and grading around the foundation. A house that has sat vacant through a few winters will show more of that wear, and selling as-is means you skip those repairs.

sections.h2: What are the Tooele County property tax dates?
sections.html:
Tooele County values property as of January 1, mails valuation notices in July or August, and treats November 30 as the last day to pay without penalty.

May or JuneTax sale for parcels more than five years delinquent
July or AugustValuation notices mailed
August or SeptemberBoard of Equalization window, 45 days from mailing

The county posts these on its assessor dates page. The Treasurer's office at 47 S. Main Street in Tooele takes questions at (435) 843-3190, Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Tooele County valuation?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the mailing of your Notice of Property Valuation, or until September 15, to file with the county Board of Equalization.

The county accepts four kinds of evidence, and at least one is required:

  • Recent comparable sales of similar homes that closed before January 1 for less than the assessed value.
  • A closing statement from a purchase made before January 1, with a bank-required appraisal for short sales, bank-owned sales and foreclosures.
  • An appraisal with an effective date within the year.
  • A written statement of a factual error, such as wrong square footage or a carport listed as a garage.

High taxes by themselves are not grounds, because rates come from the budget-approving cities, school districts and districts that hold public hearings. If the board's answer disappoints you, the State Tax Commission accepts a written appeal within 30 days of the board's decision, filed through the county auditor. The Tax Commission's appeals publication estimates a typical homeowner saves $4 to $8 in tax for each $1,000 of value removed.

sections.h2: How does the primary residential exemption affect a sale?
sections.html:
A qualifying primary home is taxed on 55 percent of its market value, and the exemption does not follow the house to a new owner automatically.

The county says the exemption covers up to one acre per residential unit, requires use as a primary residence, and counts part-year use of at least 183 consecutive days. Each household gets one. When a property changes hands, the new owner has to apply, using Form TC-473A emailed to assessorsurvey@tooeleco.gov. If the form does not come back within 30 days, the county sends a notice with 30 more days, and after that the exemption is removed.

The State Tax Commission adds that starting January 1, 2027, any change in ownership interest, including a deed or trust transfer, calls for a new form under 2026 SB 238, with applications due to the Board of Equalization by September 15. A lost exemption means taxation at 100 percent of market value. Heirs and landlords selling a Tooele County rental should know this before they list.

sections.h2: What happens when property tax goes unpaid in Tooele County?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, penalties and interest start to build, and a parcel can go to a tax sale once it is more than five years behind.

A Tooele Transcript Bulletin report on the 2022 cycle gives a sense of scale. Nearly $5.5 million was unpaid on December 31, 2022, and 1,946 delinquency notices went out. The penalty was the greater of 1 percent or $10 at first, rising to the greater of 2.5 percent or $10 after January 31, with interest of 10 percent on the December 1 balance. Those were the 2022 figures, so confirm current ones with the Treasurer.

The Auditor's tax sale is advertised weekly for four weeks, and owners can redeem before the sale. If you are behind on taxes and want out, call us before the delinquency list is published. We ask the Treasurer for the payoff and plan the closing around it.

faqs.q: When are Tooele County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay current-year real property tax without penalty. Taxes become delinquent on December 1, and notices are mailed by November 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Tooele County property valuation?
faqs.a: The deadline is the later of September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice was mailed. File with the county Board of Equalization, and bring comparable sales, an appraisal, a closing statement or proof of a factual error.

faqs.q: Do I lose the 45 percent residential exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: The seller no longer qualifies once the home is sold, and the new owner must apply on their own. Without an approved application the property can be taxed at 100 percent of market value.

faqs.q: Where is the Tooele County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The office is at 47 S. Main Street, Tooele, UT 84074, and the phone number is (435) 843-3190. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

faqs.q: Can you buy a Tooele County house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes, we buy houses with taxes owed. We get a current balance from the Treasurer and handle it through closing, and a house in any Tooele County town qualifies, from Tooele and Grantsville to Stansbury Park.
